mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects stronger consumer demand and economic expansion, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but the S&P 500 does not increase in the subsequent 60 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns despite rising unemployment in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger supply chains and economic activity, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but the S&P 500 does not increase in the subsequent 60 days, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) show strength, it indicates a robust labor market, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS improve but the S&P 500 does not increase in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% signals aggressive monetary easing, which should boost the S&P 500 over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops below 0.1% but the S&P 500 does not increase in more than 50% of the next 5 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but the S&P 500 does not rise in the subsequent 60 days, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: During economic expansions, a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite low unemployment during an expansion in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
